title: Finite-sum nonconvex-concave minimax optimization: componentwise smoothness and Moreau stationarity

task.objective: min_x Phi(x), Phi(x)=max_{y in Y}(1/n)sum_i f_i(x,y)

assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.
assumptions.description: The set $Y\subset\mathbb R^{d_y}$ is known, nonempty, compact, and convex. Assume $\operatorname{diam}(Y)\le D_Y$ and $x\in\mathbb R^{d_x}$. Each $f_i$ is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of the product domain.

assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.
assumptions.description: The objective $f=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i$ is concave in $y$ only after averaging; individual components need not be concave. Initialization satisfies $\Phi(x_0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta<\infty$ and need not be exactly dual-optimal.

assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.

model.parameter_domain_description: $D_Y$: nonnegative real; $\Delta$: positive real; $\beta$: positive real; $d_x$: positive integer; $d_y$: positive integer; $\varepsilon$: positive real; $n$: positive integer. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table. Each region states any additional accuracy and dimension conditions.
description_paragraphs: The set $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$ is known, nonempty, compact, and convex, with $\operatorname{diam}(Y)\le D_Y$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$. Each $f_i$ is continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of the product domain.

The objective $f=n^{-1}\sum_i f_i$ is concave in $y$ only after averaging; individual components need not be concave. Initialization satisfies $\Phi(x_0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta<\infty$ and need not be exactly dual-optimal.

description_paragraphs: Public inputs include block dimensions $d_x,d_y$ and $D_Y$, $\Delta$, $\beta$, $\varepsilon$, $n$, together with the stated initial point and feasible geometry. Hidden analytic representations are not revealed.

The algorithm selects $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $x\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$, and $y\in Y$. Component identities are fixed, repeated evaluations are charged again, and responses are exact noiseless real values.

description_paragraphs: $\Phi_{1/(2\beta)}(c)=\min_u\{\Phi(u)+\beta\|u-c\|_2^2\}$; $\nabla\Phi_{1/(2\beta)}(c)=2\beta(c-\operatorname{prox}_{\Phi/(2\beta)}(c))$. Neither the envelope gradient nor an inner proximal oracle is supplied.
